topic: multi-agent planning; embodied LLM agents; agent memory; reliability
status: candidate research opportunity from three cross-year full-text audits and one citation-follow-up full-text audit; bounded, not a prevalence or novelty claim
claim: The sampled agent_reliability_security evidence does not support a single generic reliability score: communication savings from plan repair depend on coordination and failure type; visual planning success depends on simulator task validity and does not establish physical reliability; and long-term memory gains in task completion/token use do not establish correct rejection of stale premises. A useful evaluation opportunity is a matched, multi-session benchmark that measures task success, failure recovery, stale-state action, and resource cost under controlled environment changes.
positive_evidence: AAMAS 2012 full paper reports plan-repair message counts averaging 59% and 43% of replanning in tightly coordinated three-agent logistics/action-failure experiments.
EMNLP 2023 VP2 reports stronger simulator benchmark results than the compared baselines on VizALF and VirtualHome.
FlowState v2 reports improved selected MemoryArena task outcomes and 43.2% lower token use than full-context on the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash backbone.
STALE provides expert-validated cases and human-judge agreement evidence, offering a concrete way to test stale-memory failures separately from retrieval or task completion.
counterevidence: The 2012 repair paper also reports diminished/no advantage in some loosely coordinated or state-perturbation settings and limits its implementation to plans with at most two coordination landmarks.

The 2023 visual-planning paper identifies many impossible ALFWorld evaluation tasks due to low-level action implementation errors and explicitly says the simulator scenarios are less complex than the real world.
FlowState's tau3-Bench Retail action accuracy falls 4.9 points while other success-related metrics improve; its authors explicitly say benchmark results do not establish deployment safety.
STALE tests a controlled one-shot conflict pair and uses LLM-generated scenarios followed by expert validation, so its result does not establish failure frequency in organic real-user histories.

sources.sections: §3-5; Appendix A limitations and E human validation

falsifiable_test: Use matched multi-session tool tasks with controlled state updates, stale-premise queries, injected tool/action failures, and communication/token budgets. Compare full-context, retrieval memory, explicit state tracking, and state adjudication. Pre-register task completion, stale/unsafe action, failure recovery, token/message costs, held-out scenarios, and multi-seed analyses. The opportunity weakens if existing independent studies already measure these endpoints jointly under comparable tasks and show transfer beyond simulation.
limitations: Only three of eight currently unread random keys in this topic are full-text audited in this batch; the fourth inspected item is abstract-only. The four full-text works use different benchmarks and estimands. This is not a systematic review, and it does not establish how often any failure occurs in deployed systems.
